data.about: A lenticular (lens-shaped) truss under equal loads at its five panel points. The lens is form-found from the force diagram: every web point of the Cremona diagram lies on one vertical line, so every panel keeps the same horizontal chord force, each vertical carries exactly half its load, and every diagonal carries nothing. Drag P to flatten or deepen the lens, and add the extra load Q to see the diagonals wake up.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: a span between two supports with five equal panel loads to carry — the dotted verticals are the loads' lines of action; the truss will be SHAPED to fit the forces
steps.title: The problem

steps.caption: left: G₁ … G₅ above the panel points — right: laid off tip-to-tail down the load line
steps.title: The loads — in both diagrams

steps.caption: right: any pole o′ with rays to the load points — left: a trial funicular from F₀ across the action lines
steps.title: Trial pole o′

steps.caption: left: the outer trial strings extended (dashed) meet on R's line of action at midspan — right: R = ΣG spans the whole load line; dashed green in BOTH diagrams
steps.title: The resultant R

steps.caption: left: dashed closing F₀–F₆ — right: the parallel through o′ cuts the load line at i
steps.title: Closing line → division point i

steps.caption: i splits the load line: A = i→LL₀ above, B = LL₅→i below, drawn on an offset line — left: A and B push up under the supports
steps.title: The reactions A and B

steps.caption: left: pick the first top node P on its rail; P′ mirrors it below the axis — chords 1 and 16 — right: through LL₀ ∥ 1 and through i ∥ 16 meet at S₂
steps.title: Choose the lens: drag P

steps.caption: right: S₂ lands exactly at MID-height of A — both end chords take the same share f₁ (marked twice) — left: that is the mirror condition l₁ = l₂
steps.title: Why symmetric? l₁ = l₂

steps.caption: left: chord 2 runs to the next action line, the vertical 7 drops to P′ — right: force 2 through LL₁ meets the web vertical at F₂: member 7 carries exactly G₁/2
steps.title: Panel 2: top chord + vertical

steps.caption: left: chord 17 from P′ — right: its force through i closes joint P′; the equal shares f₂ mark the chords' vertical components
steps.title: Panel 2: bottom chord

steps.caption: left: chords 3–6 and 18–21 with verticals 9, 11, 13, 15 — right: the whole Cremona: every web point on ONE vertical (constant horizontal force), every vertical force = half its load
steps.title: Repeat for every panel

steps.caption: left: diagonals 8, 10, 12, 14 complete the truss — right: their forces are POINTS (zero) — the lens was shaped so the uniform load needs no diagonals
steps.title: The diagonals carry nothing

steps.caption: blue = compression (top chord + verticals), pink = tension (bottom chord) — drag P, then raise factorQ: the extra load Q wakes the diagonals up
steps.title: Compression and tension
